name: tonic-prost
description: End-to-end reference: tonic 0.14 transport with the prost codec (tonic-interop binary); server-only because no prost load generator exists

upstream_pin.notes: Exact versions resolved in tests/interop/tonic/Cargo.lock; build with --locked

transport_contract.mechanism: tonic-interop server defaults; unlike tonic-pbrs this server is not passed through the rpc-bench native-matched transport settings, so nodelay/window/frame terms are peer defaults recorded per run

client.reason: No prost load generator exists (tonic-interop only runs named interop cases, not the rpc-bench workload). The matrix fails tonic-prost client cells explicitly instead of substituting the pbrs codec.

matching_configuration.cores: matched pinned cores; effective quota recorded per run
matching_configuration.http2_windows: tonic-interop server defaults (not passed through the native-matched transport contract; recorded per run)
matching_configuration.message_limits: tonic-interop server defaults; 4 MiB native-side worker body cap
matching_configuration.deadlines: interop server defaults; 5 s native-side worker deadline
matching_configuration.handler_work: same TestService procedures and payloads as native; prost decode/encode in place of pbrs

tls.reason: rpc-bench has no TLS for the tonic transport: tonic 0.14 TLS pulls a C crypto provider, conflicting with the pure-Rust dependency policy (QG-04). TLS cells touching tonic-prost are unsupported with this reason, never silently plaintext.
